A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MedAgent-Pro and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting a reliable comparison. All 15 pages of each were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original diagnostic benchmark results and ablations in Section 4, plus clinician evaluations in Section 5.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark comparisons, ablation results, and clinician evaluations in Sections 4–5.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same disease-level RAG planning, patient-level tool use, evidence-status checks, and weighted diagnostic decision procedure. No method component changes.

E1.justification: Both evaluate glaucoma using REFUGE2, heart disease using MITEA, 12 chest X-ray subtasks using MIMIC, and diverse diagnostic cases using NEJM. Clinician-evaluation task coverage also remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical VLM, medical-agent, challenge-team, and task-specific comparator sets. Table 5 still compares GPT-4o and VisionUnite. The newly cited SEINE work is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The dataset sampling, three-slice MITEA input procedure, shared GPT-4o backbone for agent comparisons, evaluation metrics, and clinician-rating protocols are unchanged in Sections 4–5.

E4.justification: Both retain the component and qualitative-model ablations in Tables 4–5, segmentation-accuracy analysis in Figure 5, fusion-strategy comparison in Figure 6, and the same diagnostic case studies and workflow analyses.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 retains ten repetitions of MITEA slice sampling and reporting of mean performance. No repeated-run, seed, uncertainty-reporting, or significance-testing information changes.

E6.justification: All result entries and plotted findings are retained. For example, MedAgent-Pro still reports 90.4% glaucoma bAcc, 77.8% heart-disease bAcc, and 81.7% overall NEJM accuracy in Table 1, and 72.0% average MIMIC bAcc in Table 2.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and their definitions of planning steps, evidence-status conditions, and weighted risk scoring are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about hierarchical evidence-based diagnosis, superiority over existing model and agent baselines, and clinical relevance. The claimed novelty and contribution scope do not change.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning quantitative indicators, structured fusion, and clinical-workflow alignment remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning visual-tool availability and VLM inconsistency and hallucination.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same GPT-4o and LangChain implementation, MedlinePlus retrieval setup, JSON/Python plan interface, and code-access statement. No implementation or reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds SEINE: Structure encoding and interaction network for nuclei instance segmentation to the segmentation citations, appearing as reference 52 in v3. The other 98 references are retained, without substantive changes to research positioning.

P1.justification: The author line changes Linghai Cai to Linghan Cai, the arXiv version/date stamp updates, and citations are renumbered after the added reference. The scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added reference produces limited bibliography reflow across pages 13–15; for example, the VisionUnite reference moves from page 14 to page 15. Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–5 retain their designs, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 updates an author-name spelling and adds one segmentation reference, with corresponding citation renumbering and bibliography reflow. These limited editorial and bibliographic changes leave the paper's explanations, empirical support, limitations, and reproducibility essentially unchanged.
